phenomena.description: The Yara-ma-yha-who is a small, red, vampire-like humanoid of southeastern Australian Aboriginal folklore, depicted with suckers on its hands and feet that drain a victim's blood; it serves as a cautionary figure warning against wandering alone beneath wild fig trees.
phenomena.origin: The legend is recorded from Aboriginal traditions of southeastern Australia. Published English-language compilations do not consistently localise it to a single nation; the story circulates in the broader cultural region documented in early-20th-century ethnographies.

phenomena.name: Yeren
phenomena.description: The Yeren (Chinese: 野人, 'wild man') is a hairy bipedal hominid cryptid reported from the remote mountain forests of central China, most famously the Shennongjia Forestry District of Hubei Province. It is the principal Chinese counterpart to Bigfoot and the Yeti.

aliases.name: Xingxing
aliases.meaning: early-text term often grouped with wildman / orang-utan-like beings

aliases.name: Feifei
aliases.meaning: fast-moving wild creature in early Chinese texts

phenomena.origin: Reports concentrate in the rugged, forested mountains of central China, especially the Shennongjia Forestry District in northwestern Hubei Province and adjacent Fang County. Additional reports come from Shaanxi (notably referenced in Yuan Mei's 1788 Zibuyu) and from a 1962 Chinese Academy of Sciences investigation in the Xishuangbanna Dai Autonomous Prefecture of Yunnan.

phenomena.name: Yeti
phenomena.description: An ape-like humanoid cryptid said to inhabit the high Himalayas of Nepal, Tibet, Bhutan, and adjacent regions. Central to Sherpa, Tibetan, and Lepcha tradition long before Western contact, the Yeti became a global cryptozoological icon after 20th-century mountaineering expeditions reported tracks and encounters.

aliases.name: Abominable Snowman
aliases.meaning: Popularized 1921 by columnist Henry Newman as a translation of metoh-kangmi

aliases.name: Dzu-teh
aliases.meaning: Cattle bear; usually identified with the Himalayan brown bear

phenomena.origin: The Yeti is reported across the Himalayan and adjacent ranges, particularly in Nepal (Khumbu, Solu, Mustang, Makalu-Barun), the Tibet Autonomous Region of China, Bhutan (where the migoi is the national cryptid), Sikkim and other northern Indian states, and parts of southern Siberia where related 'wild man' traditions exist.

phenomena.name: Yowie
phenomena.description: The Yowie is an Australian hairy bipedal hominid cryptid with deep roots in Aboriginal oral tradition and a continuous record of European-language sightings stretching back to the 19th century. It is widely treated as the Australian counterpart of Bigfoot.

aliases.name: Yō-wī
aliases.meaning: a spirit that roams the earth at night (rec. Ridley 1875)

regions: Queensland (Gold Coast hinterland, Springbrook, Gympie, Cape York)
New South Wales (Blue Mountains, NSW south coast, north coast)
phenomena.origin: Reports occur across most of mainland Australia, with the heaviest contemporary clustering in southeast Queensland (notably the Gold Coast hinterland and Springbrook), the Blue Mountains and Brindabella Ranges of New South Wales and the Australian Capital Territory, and pockets of the Northern Territory. Aboriginal traditions of comparable beings are recorded across the continent.

phenomena.name: Yuki-onna
phenomena.description: Yuki-onna ('snow woman') is a yokai of Japanese folklore who appears on snowy nights as a tall, pale, beautiful woman in a white kimono. She personifies winter and death by hypothermia, and is famous in the West through Lafcadio Hearn's 'Kwaidan' (1904).
regions: Tōhoku (Aomori, Yamagata, Akita, Iwate, Miyagi, Fukushima)
phenomena.origin: Yuki-onna traditions are concentrated in the snow-country of northern and central Japan, especially in prefectures with heavy winter snowfall: Niigata (the historical Echigo Province), Aomori, Yamagata, Akita, Miyagi, Fukushima, Iwate, Gunma, Fukui, Ibaraki, and Ehime, among others.

phenomena.name: Zmey (Slavic Dragon)
phenomena.description: The zmey (Russian zmei, Ukrainian zmiy, Polish żmij, Serbian/Croatian/Slovenian zmaj, Bulgarian zmei) is the dragon of Slavic mythology — a flying, often multi-headed, fire-breathing serpent that shapeshifts between dragon and human form, with sharply different moral roles in East Slavic and South Slavic traditions.

aliases.name: Zmey Gorynych
aliases.meaning: the Serpent Gorynych — multi-headed dragon of the bylinas

regions: East Slavic lands (Russian and Ukrainian folktale and bylina traditions)
Western Balkans (Serbian, Croatian, Slovenian zmaj traditions)
Bulgaria and North Macedonia (zmei and lamia traditions)
Poland (żmij and the Wawel Dragon of Kraków)
phenomena.origin: Pan-Slavic. The zmey is documented across the Slavic-speaking world: East Slavic (Russia, Ukraine, Belarus), South Slavic (Bulgaria, Serbia, Croatia, North Macedonia, Slovenia), and West Slavic (Poland, Czech, Slovak) traditions, with related figures in Romania.
